2.content:
This SOW covers Google’s Silicon COT Supply Chain implementation, using a global template approach to standardize core processes, incorporate required local variations, and support deployment across the agreed delivery landscape over an 18-month term.

- Establish a global design and baseline template for Silicon COT supply chain processes, supported by design workshops, governance structure, and stakeholder sign-off.
- Configure, integrate, test, and deploy the solution in phased releases, including data mapping, loading, validation, and hypercare support.
- Drive organizational readiness through change management, training planning, and structured stakeholder participation across key sites and teams.

Deferred scope decisions, assumptions, and open commercial or delivery dependencies are identified in Section 10 (Key Assumptions) and Section 21 (Key Observations).

3.1.content: Google is implementing a Silicon COT supply chain model to standardize core supply chain processes across AOI manufacturing and distribution plants while accommodating required local variations by plant, business, and legal entity. The current landscape requires clearer definition of front-end and back-end process flows, enterprise structure, master data, and transaction coverage across foundry and OSAT operations, including subcontracting, yield recording, and batch or lot traceability from wafer lot through finished goods. The engagement also addresses integration and data-flow gaps across SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, E2Open, and related boundary systems, with specific focus on forecast, purchase order, commit-message, and genealogy-related data exchanges. The business drivers are to establish a validated global design, improve master data harmonization and governance, define execution-ready technical mappings, and enable phased deployment with coordinated testing, stakeholder sign-off, and organizational readiness.

3.2.content:
- Establish an AS-IS baseline for Silicon COT supply chain processes, system interactions, and organizational structure.
- Define a global template for core processes using industry best practices and agreed localization requirements.
- Confirm the TO-BE design for subcontracting, traceability, master data, and transactional flows across the Silicon BU landscape.
- Define end-to-end data flows and integration requirements across SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, E2Open, and other in-scope systems.
- Harmonize master data, organizational structures, and governance requirements needed to support the COT operating model.
- Develop a sprint-based execution plan with agreed scope, priorities, milestones, dependencies, and ownership.
- Validate the design, scope, and delivery approach through structured workshops, playback sessions, and stakeholder sign-off.

3.3.content:
The target state is a standardized global Silicon COT supply chain process anchored in a common template and governed through centralized design, regional ownership, and coordinated execution. The future-state flow begins with discovery of current front-end and back-end operations, baseline integration schemas, and enterprise structure, then progresses through TO-BE process blueprinting, technical and functional mapping, validation of data flows and transformation logic, and phased execution planning. In the target model, planning and supply collaboration inputs flow through the defined integration landscape into SAP S/4HANA, supporting subcontracting, lot traceability, yield and cost visibility, and reporting across foundry, OSAT, and distribution operations. Local variations are incorporated within the approved global template rather than managed as separate process models.

4.1.content:
The engagement covers the Silicon business unit operating model for the in-scope manufacturing and supply locations in Taiwan and the connected Google supply chain nodes. Countries and regions in scope are:
- Taiwan: TSMC, KYEC, and SPIL plant and partner interactions.
- North America: Google Hub and warehouse operations supporting the Silicon COT supply chain.
- Delivery model: onsite support in North America and offshore delivery for designated workstreams, consistent with the agreed delivery location.

4.2.content:
The process scope covers end-to-end Silicon COT supply chain processes required to establish planning, execution visibility, and traceability across foundry, OSAT, and downstream supply operations. In-scope processes include:
- AS-IS discovery and fit-gap assessment for current front-end and back-end supply chain flows.
- TO-BE design for subcontracting and customer owned tooling supply chain operations.
- Constrained supply planning with yield-aware planning inputs.
- Forecast, purchase order, commit-message, and capacity collaboration flows across trading partners.
- Material master alignment and related master data harmonization for planning and execution.
- Batch and lot traceability from wafer lot through finished goods.
- Production planning and materials management process alignment in SAP S/4HANA.
- Integration-aligned planning flows between E2Open, SAP S/4HANA, and Kinaxis.
- Execution planning for phased deployment, validation, and go-live support.

4.3.content:
The technical scope includes the design, configuration, and enablement work required to support the Silicon COT process model across the approved application landscape. In-scope technical components include:
- SAP S/4HANA configuration for Production Planning and Materials Management process support.
- Kinaxis setup to support supply planning, constraint planning, inventory planning, analytics, and data consumption from connected systems.
- Use of Google’s existing integration framework where applicable, with incremental delta interfaces in scope based on discovery outcomes.
- BTP-IS based delta integration between SAP S/4HANA and E2Open.
- Integration design for forecast, purchase order, commit, capacity, WIP snapshot, wafer plan, yield, resource master, and unit-of-measure related data flows.
- Adaptation of the existing data template to support Silicon planning requirements.
- Functional specifications for approved custom development.
- Technical mapping for traceability, planning inputs, and boundary-system data exchange.
- `<TECH TEAM: confirm whether ABAP, analytics, PLM, and MES/Test Hub scope are included for build in this SOW or limited to assessment/design after Explore phase>`

4.4.content:
Bristlecone will provide the implementation services required to design, build, validate, and deploy the in-scope solution in a phased Agile model spanning Explore, Build, and Deploy. Services include:
- Project management, execution tracking, issue escalation, and cutover coordination.
- Discovery workshops, AS-IS assessment, and fit-gap analysis.
- TO-BE process design and business process design documentation.
- Solution configuration and build for approved in-scope functions.
- Functional specification development for custom development items.
- Test planning and execution, including unit testing, system integration testing, regression testing, performance testing, and UAT support.
- Data migration planning, mapping, loading, and validation support.
- Cutover planning and execution support.
- Hypercare support following deployment.
- Organization change management, train-the-trainer support, and knowledge transfer to the support team.

4.5.content:
The application scope covers the platforms and functional areas required to support Silicon COT planning, execution visibility, and traceability. In-scope applications and functionalities are:
- Kinaxis: Supply Planning, Constraint Planning, Inventory Planning, Analytics and Reporting, and Data Integration.
- SAP S/4HANA: Production Planning (PP), Materials Management (MM), and process integration required for the approved scope.
- E2Open: collaboration and data exchange flows supporting forecast, purchase order, commit, capacity, and contract manufacturer interactions.
- Supporting boundary integrations connected to the Silicon Hub operating model, including approved interfaces to analytics and engineering data sources where confirmed in design.

5.content:
The solution architecture uses SAP S/4HANA as the system of record for core Production Planning and Materials Management processes, Kinaxis for supply, constraint, and inventory planning, and E2Open for external collaboration flows with foundry and OSAT partners. The architecture supports forecast, purchase order, commit, capacity, WIP, wafer-plan, yield, unit-of-measure, and approved boundary-system data exchanges required for the Silicon COT operating model.

The deployment model follows a phased implementation across Explore, Build, and Deploy, using the approved global template as the design baseline and incorporating local variations within that template. Existing Google integration capabilities will be retained where applicable, with incremental delta integration delivered through BTP-IS between SAP S/4HANA and E2Open and detailed interface validation completed during Explore.

The target design supports lot-level traceability across E2Open and SAP S/4HANA, with boundary control between lot-level collaboration data and unit-level test or analytics data. It also incorporates the required enterprise structure, master data, subcontracting, yield recording, genealogy, and reporting components needed to support Taiwan manufacturing partners and connected Google supply chain nodes.

Change governance will be managed through structured design workshops, playback sessions, stakeholder review, and formal sign-off against the global template, technical mappings, and phased release scope. Any architecture changes affecting integrations, custom development, deployment sequencing, or commercial effort will be routed through the agreed change control process. `<TECH TEAM: confirm whether an approved solution architecture diagram should be inserted here from the source material or drafted separately>`

6.1.content:
Bristlecone will deliver the engagement through a phased implementation model across Explore, Realize, Deploy, and Run, with project management and governance operating throughout. Explore will confirm the AS-IS baseline, complete fit-gap assessment, validate localization requirements, finalize the global solution design, and update the project plan, charter, design documents, and RICEFW list as required. Realize will cover configuration, approved custom development, unit testing, mock data loads, and security implementation. Deploy will cover system integration testing, user acceptance testing, train-the-trainer activities, end-user readiness, cutover planning, go/no-go governance, data migration execution, and production go-live. Run will cover post-go-live support, transition, knowledge transfer, project closure, and lessons learned.

The rollout will follow phased capability releases aligned to agreed business priorities, starting with initial procurement and collaboration enablement, then expanding to wafer-to-finished-goods planning capability and subsequent approved scope increments. Localization will be incorporated within the approved global template and validated through structured review and sign-off before build proceeds.

7.1.content:
The engagement will be governed through a three-tier model comprising executive steering oversight, program management control, and workstream delivery governance. The executive sponsors will provide direction on scope, funding, priorities, and milestone decisions. The Program Manager will lead day-to-day governance, coordinate cross-functional and cross-system dependencies, maintain the integrated plan, and escalate risks, issues, and decisions requiring client action. Functional, integration, data, and business stakeholders will participate in design reviews, sprint checkpoints, test readiness reviews, and deployment planning.

Escalation will follow the delivery path from workstream leads to the Program Manager, then to the client solution architect and sponsor group where timeline, scope, budget, or cross-team decisions are required. Governance cadence will include weekly project status reviews, sprint planning and review sessions, risk and issue reviews, milestone decision checkpoints, and executive steering reviews at agreed stage gates.

7.3.content:
- Delivery will follow an 18-month phased implementation aligned to Explore, Build, Test, Deploy, and Hypercare activities.
- The indicative work sequence is blueprinting and design, configuration, integration and data mapping, loading and validation, SIT, UAT, performance testing, deployment, and hypercare.
- Core governance and delivery activities will run on a sprint-based cadence with weekly status reviews and regular planning, review, and dependency checkpoints.
- Onsite coverage will support governance, workshops, milestone reviews, and deployment coordination in North America; offshore teams will execute designated build, integration, testing, and data activities.
- Google business and technical SMEs will provide participation across design validation, data mapping, test execution, sign-off, and deployment readiness at the levels required by each project phase.
- Detailed working hours, holiday calendars, and any shift coverage requirements will be aligned during mobilization and documented in the project plan.

8.content:
- Personnel assigned to this engagement shall have working proficiency in English and be able to conduct design workshops, playback sessions, issue resolution, testing support, and governance discussions with Google stakeholders across onsite and offshore teams.

- Team members shall have implementation experience in semiconductor or complex discrete-manufacturing supply chain environments, including planning, subcontracting, traceability, master data, and integration-led execution across foundry, OSAT, and distribution operations.

- Functional resources shall be familiar with the in-scope process areas covering demand and supply planning, inventory and constraint planning, procurement, manufacturing, quality coordination points, and SAP S/4HANA PP/MM process alignment.

- Technical and integration resources shall have hands-on experience with SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, E2Open, and connected enterprise integrations, including data mapping, loading, validation, interface design, and coordination with boundary systems such as PLM, MES/Test Hub, and analytics platforms where applicable to approved scope.

- Personnel supporting data and design activities shall be able to work with master data structures, planning inputs, traceability data, forecast and purchase-order transactions, commit and capacity messages, wafer and WIP data, yield data, and unit-of-measure conversions relevant to the Silicon COT model.

- Delivery resources shall be experienced in Agile implementation methods, fit-to-standard workshops, sprint-based execution, test-cycle support, phased deployment, and hypercare transition.

- Training and change-management personnel, where assigned, shall be capable of supporting train-the-trainer activities, stakeholder readiness, and business-user adoption for the deployed solution.

- Google shall provide or confirm named business and solution representatives for program governance, end-to-end solution design, integration and data management, key business-user participation, and sign-off support consistent with the governance model and role expectations defined elsewhere in this SOW.

- Bristlecone shall staff the engagement with qualified implementation, functional, integration, architecture, project management, and change-management personnel aligned to the approved delivery model of onsite support in North America and offshore execution.

- Certifications shall include relevant product or role-based qualifications for assigned consultants where required for delivery, including Kinaxis-certified training capability for training workstreams and comparable SAP or integration credentials for specialist roles as applicable. <CONFIRM: any client-mandated minimum certifications or background-screening requirements>`
